Read More Home About us Pratham Education Foundation (Pratham) is one of the largest NGOs in India, with a track record of innovative, rigorously evaluated programs that have inspired similar initiatives across three continents. Pratham’s journey began in 1995 in Mumbai with the mission: Every Child in School and Learning Well. From the slums of India’s biggest city to today’s presence in more than 26 states and union territories, our journey has been one of learning and scale—from evidence to practice, from small innovations to systemic reforms. Pratham’s work extends from programs for early and elementary years to initiatives for girls and women, and youth skilling. We reach 7 million children and youth in a typical year through a combination of efforts: working directly with children and youth in communities, as well as through collaborations with state and district-level governments. Read More Our Vision Pratham is committed to making schools and communities future-ready where every child, youth and woman has the education, tools, and opportunities to thrive in an ever-changing world. Our Programs Education From Early Childhood Education to Elementary Education, Pratham identifies education-related gaps and opportunities in each segment and develops context-based solutions. We collaborate with children, schools, families, and communities through direct programs and government partnerships. Read More Second Chance Vocational Training Annual Status of Education Report Reach 2025-26 KC Widget Content Activities in 24 states & union territories Children reached 7.56 through direct programs and government partnerships Girls and women reached 208 through mothers' groups and second chance program Youth reached 84 through vocational/non- vocational courses Stories Of Change Step into the heart of Pratham’s mission through our Stories of Change—a collection of real-life journeys that showcase the resilience, determination, and hope of those we serve. From children building strong learning foundations to women and youth rewriting their futures, these stories highlight the transformative power of education and skills. Explore how, together with our communities and partners, we’re creating lasting impact, one story at a time. These visionaries guide us, keep us focused on our mission, and help us deliver on our ambitious goals. Their support empowers us to continue to innovate and grow and create impact for millions of children and youth. National Board of Directors Emeritus Board Banmali Agrawala Chairman, Pratham Education Foundation Mr. Banmali Agrawala is a veteran in the energy domain. With a diverse and global experience spanning over three decades, he has spearheaded national and international organisations. Currently, he is the President, Infrastructure and Defence & Aerospace at Tata Sons Private Limited. read more Dr. Madhav Chavan Co-Founder, Pratham Education Foundation Dr. Madhav Chavan co-founded Pratham to address the problems of universal primary education in Mumbai. Since then, he has led the development of the organisation, pioneering large-scale innovations to address literacy challenges among India’s underserved children. read more Dinyar S. Devitre Vice Chairman, Pratham Education Foundation Mr. Dinyar (Dinny) S. Devitre is an international business executive who has held leadership positions over a 45-year period in the consumer products and financial services industries in Asia, Australia, Japan, Europe, and the U.S. Mr. Devitre held several senior operating positions with Philip Morris Inc. and then with Altria Group Inc. read more Jalaj Dani Mr. Jalaj Dani is currently the Director of Reliance Foundation. He is also co-promoter of Asian Paints and has spent over two decades in leadership positions within the organisation. Throughout his career, Mr. Dani has worked extensively in the areas of healthcare, education, rural transformation, sports, skilling and disaster management. read more Sonny Iqbal Mr. Sonny Iqbal helped establish Egon Zehnder’s offices in New Delhi, Bangalore, and Mumbai, and has been a Partner with the Firm for over 27 years. He co-founded Egon Zehnder’s global Family Business Advisory Practice and advises family businesses on navigating the challenges of succession, founder transition, governance, and professionalization across geographies. read more Nirmal Jain Mr. Nirmal Jain is the Promoter and Managing Director of IIFL Finance Limited and the founder of the IIFL Group. Since founding the Group in 1995, he has led its transformation into one of India’s most respected and diversified financial services institutions. read more Pramit Jhaveri Mr. Pramit Jhaveri presently acts as advisor and mentor to start ups, corporates and family offices. He is Senior Advisor to Premji Invest and PJT Partners and an Independent Director on the Boards of Bajaj Finance, Bajaj Finserv and Larsen & Toubro. read more Sanjiv Malhotra Mr. Sanjiv Malhotra brings a wealth of experience with 45 years in global banking and financial consulting. His leadership roles span corporate and commercial banking, risk management, and M&A. He’s been the Chief Risk Officer for Citigroup South Asia and Citigroup Thailand during the Asian Crisis. read more Rekha M. Menon Ms. Rekha M. Menon is a seasoned leader known for driving disruptive transformation while balancing sustainable growth. Social worker. Educationist. Economist. Activist. These are Pratham's leaders: visionaries dedicated to improving opportunities for children and youth in India. Here are some of the pillars of Pratham. Meenakshi Ramesh CEO, Pratham Education Foundation Meenakshi Ramesh is the Chief Executive Officer of Pratham Education Foundation. She brings over two decades of social sector leadership to her role. Her appointment marks a meaningful return to the organisation where she began her development sector journey. read more Dr. Rukmini Banerji Rukmini Banerji is a Senior Advisor to Pratham Education Foundation. She served as the organisation's CEO for more than a decade, from 2015 to 2026. With extensive experience in the design and delivery of educational interventions, she played a pivotal role in developing and implementing Pratham's partnership programs with governments. read more Farida Lambay Farida Lambay has over 40 years of experience as an educationist and social activist. She co-founded Pratham in 1995 along with Dr. Madhav Chavan. She is also the co-founder and trustee of the Pratham Mumbai Education Initiative, which runs the Pratham Council for Vulnerable Children program across India. read more Dr. Madhav Chavan Dr. Madhav Chavan is the Co-Founder of Pratham Education Foundation. After obtaining a PhD in chemistry from Ohio State University and working as a visiting faculty member at the University of Houston, he returned to India in 1986 to research and teach chemistry. However, he soon started working in the slums of Mumbai as part of the National Literacy Mission. read more Dr. Wilima Wadhwa Dr. Wilima Wadhwa has been Director of ASER Centre and, since July 2015, has taken over as Head of the Centre. She has been associated with the Annual Status of Education Report (ASER) since its inception in 2005. She is the architect of the ASER survey and other primary research studies currently undertaken by ASER Centre. read more Board Partners Board Leadership Partners Teaching at the Right Level Awards & Recognition What’s New Legal & Financial Information FEATURED VIDEO https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YGJkyw5miT0&list=PLB9QKFRqqhbMUkXTqPvpr5LQsjNl7iqFd&index=1 About Us Our story Board Leadership Awards & Recognition Programs Education Pratham-Jameel Second Chance Program Youth & Skilling Digital Initiatives Annual Status of Education Report Get Involved Work with Us Our Partners Resources Stories of Change Publications and Reports Delhi Office B- 4/59, Safdarjung Enclave 1st Floor, New Delhi - 110 029 Email: info@pratham.org Contact number: 01141651638 Mumbai Office Y.B. pages.text: Skip to content About Us Our story Board Leadership Teaching at the Right Level Awards & Recognition Media & Publications Financials Programs Education Early Years Elementary Years Hamara Gaon Inclusive Education (ENABLE) Pratham-Jameel Second Chance Program Youth & Skilling Digital Initiatives Creativity Clubs Annual Status of Education Report Get Involved Donate Work with Us Internships Our Partners Resources Pratham Digital Stories of Change Blogs Campaigns CAMaL Ki Taiyyari 2026 Daan Utsav 2025 CAMaL Ka Camp 2025 IAmPratham Publications and Reports Contact Donate Now Donate Our Partners Support Us in Amplifying Our Impact We invite organisations to collaborate with Pratham in our effort to bring about lasting change. Through partnerships with Pratham, your company and you can play a key role in shaping the future of children, youth, and women, while advancing your Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) objectives and contributing to social impact at a national level. HOW TO PARTNER WITH PRATHAM? Tailored Partnership Join us in building sustainable communities where children develop strong foundational skills, girls and women complete their secondary education, and youth access employment and entrepreneurial opportunities. Pratham offers tailored CSR partnerships that align with your company’s values and goals. Your support will help us scale impactful programs, transforming lives and fostering long-term change. Employee Volunteering Partnering with Pratham provides your employees with volunteer opportunities to engage with communities and share their expertise. These experiences cultivate a culture of social responsibility within your organisation, inspiring employees to give back to society. These volunteering opportunities also serve as a valuable team-building exercise for your employees. Employee Giving Encouraging your employees to support a cause of their choice not only demonstrates your company’s commitment to social responsibility but also fosters a culture of giving within the organisation. Employees can participate in payroll giving with us or make individual contributions through this link . To know more on how your organisation can partner with Pratham, please reach out to our Corporate Partnerships team at info@pratham.org . WHAT CAN YOU PARTNER ON? CHILDREN AND LEARNING Our programs are designed to ensure that children acquire strong foundational literacy and numeracy skills. Your support will help us scale our ongoing efforts like the Ea rly Years program , H amara Gaon or our work with children in elementary grades . YOUTH AND SKILLING Through our Skilling program , your company can equip youth (18-25 years) from economically disadvantaged backgrounds with skills that enhance their employability and provide them with job opportunities. GIRLS AND WOMEN Pratham’s Second Chance program helps girls and women complete their secondary education, opening gateways for them to lifelong learning and earning opportunities. With your support, they can build a brighter future. DIGITAL INITIATIVES Digital technology is an integral component of Pratham’s programs. We are committed to building tech-enabled solutions that leverage emerging technologies like AI to help children, youth, and women to prepare them for school, work, and life. Support us to build innovative products and programs to reach the last mile. OUR PARTNERS AND SUPPORTERS ITC Limited Since 2013, Pratham and ITC have developed a long-standing partnership to improve educational outcomes for children aged 3-14 and provide skill training to people aged 18-35 across 12 states in India. Read More Vodafone Idea Foundation Pratham and Vodafone Idea Foundation began its collaboration in 2012 to improve student learning outcomes through technology integration into classrooms. AG-01.name: About-page concreteness
AG-01.finding_requires: a packet page reference (E...), the exact passage read, and which of who / offering / category it leaves unanswered

AG-02.name: Independent mentions
AG-02.finding_requires: the queries executed, each with its result count (zero allowed), and the identity the searches used; scoped to those searches

AG-03.name: Independent contradiction
AG-03.finding_requires: the exact site claim with its packet reference, an inspected conflicting page with URL and quote, why it is the same entity, date or context, and whether the conflict is material

AG-04.name: Facts drawn inside images
AG-04.finding_requires: an image candidate reference (I...) that was actually viewed, the fact transcribed from it, and why the page text does not state it

AG-05.name: Namesake ambiguity
AG-05.finding_requires: the competing entities observed, each with a URL and the fact that distinguishes it from the brand

AG-06.name: Review and profile opportunity
